title: Arrow functions - fn() syntax and automatic capture
keywords: how to write an arrow function
answer: Arrow functions are one-expression closures written with fn. They capture variables from the surrounding scope automatically, by value. They cannot contain multiple statements, so anything longer than one expression needs a full closure.
pitfall: An arrow function cannot have a statement body or a return keyword. fn($n) => { return $n; } is a parse error.

title: Closures and callbacks - anonymous functions and use()
answer: A closure is a function without a name, stored in a variable. It cannot see outside variables unless you list them in use(). Since PHP 7.4, arrow functions capture outside variables automatically, by value.
pitfall: use() copies the variable's value at definition time. Changing the outer variable later does not change what the closure sees, unless you capture by reference with use (&$var).

title: Variadic functions and named arguments
answer: A ... parameter collects any number of extra arguments into an array. Named arguments let callers pass values by parameter name, in any order, which makes calls with many optional settings readable.
pitfall: A variadic parameter must be the last parameter. Putting another parameter after ... is a parse error.
